newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Decision expected on U.S. arms to Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Decision expected on U.S. arms to Bosnia.

text.p: The American military contractor hired to oversee U.S. arms deliveries to the Bosnian army despatched a team to the Croatian port of Ploce on Friday to prepare for possible off-loading of a huge shipment.

"We have a group of people in Ploce today checking out the port facilities to be certain everything is ready if the cargo is released," Joseph Allred, spokesman for the contractor, Military Professional Resources Inc. (MPRI), told Reuters.

A cargo vessel has been idling in the Adriatic since October 24th with tanks, helicopters, automatic rifles, machine-guns and ammunition bound for Bosnia for weeks, but the delivery has been blocked by a political dispute with Sarajevo.

The U.S. government has vowed not to deliver the military equipment until Sarajevo dismisses the Moslem-Croat federation's deputy defence minister, Hasan Cengic. The U.S. objects to Cengic's close ties with Iran.
Iran supplied weapons and ammunition to Sarajevo during the 43-month Bosnian war in violation of the U.N. arms embargo. The United States knew of the deliveries but did not object.
Since the war ended with the Dayton peace agreement last year Washington has worked hard to sever Bosnian ties to Iran, whose government it accuses of sponsoring state terrorism.
The U.S. made its sponsorship of the "train and equip" programme contingent upon departure of foreign Islamic fighters, known as mujahedin, from Bosnia.
Bosnian sources said Cengic, a Moslem, and Vladimir Soljic, the federation defence minister, were both likely to be sacked over the weekend in what will be billed as a reorganisation.
